newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil ports back to normal after ending strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil ports back to normal after ending strike.

text.p: Brazil's key commodities' ports were operating normally this morning after ending a two-day old strike over a Congressional bill regulating inland and coastal shipping, port authority officials said.
Workers at the ports of Santos, Paranagua, Maceio and Vitoria had returned to work this morning, officials said.

Workers at the port of Recife had gone back to work yesterday after adhering only to the original proposal of a 24-hour strike while the port of Rio de Janeiro had been functioning normally throughout the stoppage.
The strike was brought to an end after lawmakers dropped a clause from the bill which would have allowed members of foreign crews to carry out tasks currently reserved for Brazilian portworkers.
The bill, which regulates the 1995 opening of the Brazilian inland shipping sector to foreign firms, was passed by the Lower House on Wednesday and must now be approved by the Senate.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
